AiStatus.description: Whether this deployment can call Claude at all.

BaseScreen.description: The screen that exists in production today, when this is a change request rather than a fresh design.

BaseScreenBlock.description: One block of the live screen being revised.

CanvasBlockView.description: One block of the canvas being edited.

catalog.description: The block catalogue, rendered by the client. This is what tells the model which kinds and props exist.

projectId.description: Attributes the spend to a project.

CanvasEditResponse.description: The model's proposed operations, unvalidated against the catalogue — the client checks them before applying.

dataBase64.description: Images only — base64 with no data: prefix.

text.description: Text files only — their content, read in the browser.

effort.description: Thinking depth; ignored by models that do not take it.

thinking.description: Ask for a reasoning summary; ignored by models without it.

referenceNames.description: Names of attachments with no extractable text, so the model knows they exist.

references.description: Merged text of the meeting's reference files.

skipped.description: Screens the model proposed that this API could not read at all.

MeetingUpdate.description: Only the fields present are changed.

productId.description: Id of the product to build into; empty string clears it.

movedTo.description: The product they have actually been sent to. A fact.

product.description: The product these screens are built to fit. A plan.

Placement.description: Where a screen was agreed to sit, as the path it was agreed at. Kept as a path rather than a reference because the parent may not be in this product yet.

id.description: Supplied when the client already named it; generated otherwise.

ProjectRef.description: Just enough of a project to name it.

ProjectUpdate.description: Only the fields present are changed.

ProjectView.description: A project of either kind; archived means Customer.

id.description: The copy's own id. Generated when absent.

RequestFile.description: Filing a waiting request into a round.

RequestMove.description: Moving a set of screens into a product. A screen whose name already waits from the same source replaces that row rather than joining it.

RequestView.description: A screen waiting in a product for a round.

version.description: The round it was filed into; null while it is still waiting.

ScreenView.description: A screen without its page. The html is fetched per screen, because a meeting's pages together run to megabytes.

change.description: `new` when the product has never had it, `modified` when it changed since it was sent, null when they agree.

ScreenWrite.description: One generated screen. `parentId` may name another screen in the same request; parents need not be listed first.

ScreensMoved.description: Records that the set has been sent to a product.

ScreensReplace.description: The whole set after a generation. Screens matched by name keep their id, their placement and their moved mark; the rest are new.

UserView.description: Who the caller is, as the workspace shows them.

WorkspaceStatePatch.description: A batch of writes, applied together. The browser batches its changes and sends them as one request rather than one per key.

WorkspaceStateSnapshot.description: Everything the caller can see, as one map. Read once when the workspace loads, because the code that consumes it reads synchronously.

entries.description: Key to the exact string that was stored.

personalKeys.description: Keys that belong to this viewer rather than the team.

WorkspaceStateWrite.description: One key to write, or to delete when `value` is null.

value.description: The string to store. Null deletes the key.
